sources.license: MIT (LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2026 Daniil Ostashev, added in c6893aa24ec2b2822ef42ab695c828de1ccb9015); the README says it covers the verification code and the record packings and certificates. The retained files are byte-identical with the licence beside them. Issue #562 credits Daniil Ostashev with the three packings, names the sources of their pieces, and states AI assistance: an AI-assisted research loop the author drives with his own ideas, in which AI agents wrote and ran the search, composition and verification code, and an agent's check of the rectangle library against the register found 129.
claims: Issue #562 reports s(129) <= 11.87001385040446434457885353928463864242, s(204) <= 14.80866323438695656647099008094596479529 and s(303) <= 17.90995829106990798159574108139873608005, certified and rounded up; each records/n0NNN.sqcert gives the exact side, dilated by 1 + 1e-60 from the 60-digit optimum of its contact topology, and the README at the pin prints the same sides rounded up to 15 places.

The issue says 204 and 303 are new arrangements, compositions of two copies of a new rectangle packing in opposite corners plus aligned squares: 44 unit squares in an (h + 3) x h rectangle with h = 5.80866323438695656632... for 204, and 62 unit squares in an (h + 6) x h rectangle with h = 5.90995829106990798142... for 303, both found by a GPU soft-to-rigid search after Yohei Nakajima's idea, started from corner staircases. 129 is a cut-out of a 163-square (h + 3) x h rectangle cut from the s(302) house (Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing, Evan Daniel's regularization) and re-optimised; its aligned blocks are laid out like Ryan Xu's s(129), with its tilted squares in a different band.

The README at the pin also prints s(176) <= 13.808663234386957, a composition of issue 528's 38-square piece with the 44-square piece; the issue does not ask for it, since Francisco Couzo has improved it from this packing, and issue #575 later reports a smaller 176 of the author's own.

The author reports that its own C++ checker (sqverify) accepts all three in GMP rational arithmetic and that a separate 80-digit mpmath cross-check accepts them; each side is reported as the exact first-order optimum of its contact topology with nonnegative KKT multipliers. These are author reports; no optimality is claimed.
